According to the repository's general rules, threshold values must be explicitly verified as valid finite numbers before performing numeric comparisons (such as `>=` or `<=`) in JavaScript. This prevents comparisons against `null` (which can occur when configuration files are missing or malformed) from erroneously evaluating to `true` due to null coercion to `0`.

In this check, `coverage.missing_semantic_coverage_question_count >= 0` and `coverage.semantic_slice_universe_question_count >= coverage.semantic_slice_covered_question_count` are performed without verifying that the operands are valid finite numbers. If `coverage.missing_semantic_coverage_question_count` is `null`, `null >= 0` will evaluate to `true`, which could lead to an incorrect validation pass.

Please explicitly verify these values using `Number.isFinite()` before performing the comparisons.

```suggestion
    check('semantic_slice_coverage_and_fallback_reported', (
      Number.isFinite(coverage.semantic_slice_covered_question_count) &&
      coverage.semantic_slice_covered_question_count > 0 &&
      Number.isFinite(coverage.semantic_slice_universe_question_count) &&
      coverage.semantic_slice_universe_question_count >= coverage.semantic_slice_covered_question_count &&
      Number.isFinite(coverage.missing_semantic_coverage_question_count) &&
      coverage.missing_semantic_coverage_question_count >= 0 &&
      fallback.fallback_behavior_status === 'fallback_available_without_semantic_fact_invention'
    ), {
```
